Path from the input folder and calls .exists() / .is_dir() / .is_file() on it, and the final consolidated checkpoint is written with a plain torch.save. Both of these assumptions break for checkpoints stored in remote/object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, etc.), which have no real directory semantics and can't be addressed with pathlib. Lightning already added fsspec URL support for saving/loading distributed checkpoints in ModelParallelStrategy and for FSDP checkpoints more broadly.
